summary: Wildcard off-registry-shape dependency on PoC-named package enables install-time code execution
details: tostpro@112.5.9 declares a runtime dependency on 'abbishal-poc-as-dependency' pinned to wildcard version '*' in package.json. On npm install, this resolves and installs whatever is currently published under that name, running any lifecycle scripts and loading its code into the installer's dependency graph with no version pin and no integrity constraint. The package's own main entry (dist/index.js) prints 'poc by abbishal' and 'Hi interested in joining our team? then contact, you know how.', and the package name 'tostpro' with the 'Tellyo translations' description is consistent with a public package mimicking an internal name so that an internal build system auto-resolves it. The attack surface is the wildcard dependency: whoever controls 'abbishal-poc-as-dependency' on the registry obtains arbitrary code execution on every machine that installs tostpro.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
